Capital One.

This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, D.C., I'm Dale Willman.
Former President Barack Obama was campaigning for Democratic candidates in Ohio and Michigan
Saturday, where he was greeted by large, loud crowds of supporters shouting, "Vote, vote,
vote."
Speaking in Detroit, Obama blamed President Trump's policies for the high prices facing
consumers right now, and he said it's time for something different.
People are so ready for something new, so hungry for something better, so sick and tired
of being sick and tired, that everywhere you go it feels like change is in the air.
And Michigan, that's what I'm feeling right now.
President Trump campaigned in Georgia Saturday, where he offered his endorsement to Republican
gubernatorial candidate Brian Donalds.
He also announced that carmaker Audie has committed $4.2 billion to build a plant in
Macon, Georgia that will open in the early 2030s.
Flashes erupted in Paris Saturday as mass protests continued around that country.
As NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports, the protests had been largely peaceful through most of
the day.
Protesters of all ages and backgrounds, students, workers, members of the Yellow Vest movement,
coursed down a Paris boulevard.
Many held signs against capitalism and President Emmanuel Macron.
There were chants against the police and for taxing the rich.
Nurse Jenny Bartelemy says things are going downhill in every way.
People are eating so poo, and our children have been beaten up by the police and all
that.
So we just say stop.
TV footage showed skirmishes and tear gas in other cities such as Lyon, Marseille and
Toulouse, where protesting was banned.
Eleanor Beardsley in Pierre News, Paris.
Police reported nearly 1,000 arrests in France during those protests.
Remnants of Hurricane Trudy continue moving through the Four Corners region, bringing
with it flooding that's displaced residents Jamie Wanzek reports from Durango, Colorado.
As heavy rains in southern Colorado and northern New Mexico begin to recede, dangerous flooding
conditions remain in Farmington, New Mexico.
Devin Neely is with San Juan County.
The water in both the San Juan and Animas River is contaminated with raw sewage.
Folks need to stay out of the floodwater, and there are some severe dangers associated
with the floodwaters right now.
Farmington Utilities has shut off power in areas inundated with water.
The National Guard continues to assist with local and state crews with aerial and swift
water rescues in much of northwest New Mexico and the Navajo Nation.
For NPR News, I'm Jamie Wanzek in Durango, Colorado.
And you're listening to NPR News.
At least one person has been rescued following the collapse Friday of a building under construction
in Nairobi, Kenya.
The Kenya Red Cross says at least 31 people remain missing.
The collapse happened while the surrounding streets were filled with people, and initial
fears were that many more were buried under the rubble.
Nearby shop owners are blaming the local government for the collapse, saying they do not enforce
building regulations.
Milwaukee won Game 2 of the World Series Saturday, beating Tampa Bay 5-4 for a two-game lead.
This was an epic comeback for the Milwaukee Brewers.
Milwaukee fell behind 4-0 in the top of the first, but the Brewers never gave up.
They scored two runs in the bottom of the first, got a single run in the fourth.
Milwaukee tied the game in the sixth inning, then in the seventh.
Milwaukee finally took the lead on a single by Cooper Pratt.
Milwaukee beats Tampa Bay 5-4.
The Brewers lead the best of seven series, two games to none.
The fans here elated.
The series now heads to Florida for Game 3, 4 and, if necessary, Game 5.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Fetterman at the World Series in Milwaukee.
Golden State offered a stifling defense Saturday as they beat the Atlanta Dream 67-62 in Game
4, the WNBA Finals.
They were able to hold Dream star Angel Reist just eight points after she had averaged more
than 25 points in the previous two games.
The Finals are now tied at two games apiece.
Game 5 will take place on Monday evening.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.
